title: On dust evolution in planet-forming discs in binary systems - II. Comparison with Taurus and ρ Ophiuchus (sub-)millimetre observations: discs in binaries have small dust sizes
question: Whether theoretical models of dust evolution (grain growth and radial drift) in binary protoplanetary discs agree with ALMA (sub-)millimetre observations of disc dust sizes, tidal truncation radii, and the flux-radius correlation in Taurus and rho Ophiuchus.

data.angular_resolution: ~0.20 arcsec (rho Ophiuchus, Cox et al. 2017); ~0.12 arcsec (Taurus, Manara et al. 2019)

recipe.goal: Compile archival binary disc fluxes and fit the flux-separation correlation
recipe.method: Gather archival (sub-)mm continuum fluxes of binary pairs in Taurus, rho Ophiuchus, and Lupus, re-scale to 0.85 mm and d=140 pc, and perform a three-Gaussian hierarchical Bayesian linear regression in log space.
key_parameters: 10 chains and 2.5x10^4 steps; non-detection uncertainty assumed as 1/3 of quoted upper limit; pairs closer than 0.15 arcsec in Harris et al. (2012) excluded as circumbinary
assumptions: F_nu proportional to nu^2 between 0.85 mm and 1.33 mm; reference distance d = 140 pc

recipe.goal: Compute disc-integrated spectral indices in binaries to validate multi-band flux scaling
recipe.method: Compute spectral indices alpha_0.9-1.3mm between ALMA Band 7 (0.9 mm) and Band 6 (1.3 mm) fluxes for binary and single-star discs in Taurus, rho Ophiuchus, and Lupus.

recipe.goal: Compute synthetic Band 7 surface brightness, fluxes, and dust radii from binary disc evolution models
recipe.method: Compute 0.85 mm dust opacity via Mie theory, calculate radial surface brightness profile S_b(R) for 1D secular dust evolution models from Paper I, integrate S_b(R) to obtain total flux F, and determine radii enclosing 68% (R_68,mod) and 95% (R_95,mod) of the dust flux.
key_parameters: Wavelength = 0.85 mm (ALMA Band 7); R_in = 10^-2 au; 10^-4 <= alpha <= 0.025; 10 au <= R_0 <= 80 au; t = 0.1, 0.3, 1, 2, 3 Myr; sensitivity cut S_b = 3.33x10^8 Jy sr^-1 (7.85 mJy arcsec^-2)
assumptions: Face-on discs; d = 140 pc; compact spherical grains with 10% silicates, 30% refractory organics, 60% water ice, grain size distribution exponent q = -3.5; solar mass star

recipe.goal: Fit rho Ophiuchus binary disc continuum visibilities to measure fluxes and dust radii
recipe.method: Average continuum visibilities in each spectral window, rescale uv-distances to wavelength units, model each disc component with a power-law and exponential taper intensity profile using galario, and fit the 8*n parameter space with MCMC using emcee to derive F, R_68,obs, and R_95,obs.
key_parameters: 8 parameters per disc component (log F_tot, gamma_1, gamma_2, R_C, i, PA, Delta_alpha, Delta_delta); 100 to 300 walkers; 5x10^3 to 2x10^4 steps; last 1000 steps used for posterior median and 16th/84th percentiles
assumptions: Axisymmetric intensity profile I(R) proportional to (R/R_C)^(-gamma_1) * exp(-(R/R_C)^gamma_2); circumbinary discs excluded; Gaia distances from Williams et al. (2019)

recipe.goal: Estimate observational tidal truncation radii and compare with model and observed dust radii and dust-to-gas size ratios
recipe.method: Compute zero-eccentricity tidal truncation radii R_trunc from observed projected separations a_p and mass ratios q using the Eggleton radius formula (for Taurus) or R_trunc = a_p/3 (for rho Ophiuchus), and compare R_68 and R_95 as well as R_dust/R_gas against model predictions.
assumptions: Zero orbital eccentricity e = 0; true separation a ~ a_p; equal mass stars q = 1 for rho Ophiuchus targets; R_68,gas = 0.68*R_trunc and R_95,gas = 0.95*R_trunc

recipe.goal: Test the flux-radius correlation and its dependence on truncation radius in observations and models
recipe.method: Perform Bayesian linear regression (linmix) of log(R_68,obs) vs log(F_nu) and of log(F_nu / R_68,obs^2) vs log(R_trunc) for Taurus and rho Ophiuchus binary discs, run Spearman and Pearson correlation tests, and compare against drift-dominated models (alpha = 10^-3, 10^-4) and the Tripathi et al. (2017) single-star relation.
key_parameters: 10 chains and 2.5x10^4 steps in linmix; T Tau S and UY Aur B excluded; asymmetric error bars set to the larger error; drift-dominated models with alpha = 10^-3, 10^-4 and R_0 = 10, 30, 80 au
assumptions: F_nu proportional to nu^2 to rescale 1.33 mm Taurus fluxes to 0.85 mm; d = 140 pc; R_68,1.3mm / R_68,0.9mm ~ 1

score_reason: Archival ALMA project codes and simulation software (DiscEvolution, galario, emcee, linmix) are explicitly named and public, mathematical equations for all models and fits are fully specified, and complete fitted parameter tables for all 15 rho Ophiuchus targets are provided; minor details like MCMC prior bounds and visibility calibration scripts are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival ALMA data (2013.1.00157.S and 2016.1.01164.S), public simulation and visibility-fitting codes (DiscEvolution, galario, emcee, linmix), and explicit numeric answer keys for both the 15 visibility fits (Tables 2-3) and the Bayesian linear regressions (Tables 1-3 in main text).
